# Divergences from Prettier

<!-- Generated by `mise run oracle:divergences` from `oracle/divergences.ts` and `oracle/divergences/*.md`. Edit those, not this file. -->

Where mdtidy's Prettier preset differs from prettier@3.9.10 on purpose. Each case is a minimal input run through both. `→` is a tab and `·` is a trailing space. A _meaning_ entry is a place where Prettier's output reads differently from its input; a _layout_ entry is a choice between two outputs that read the same. Gaps that mdtidy should close, and parser bugs, are in `handoff.md` instead.

## HTML in a task item keeps its indent

`task-html`. Kind: meaning. Luke's rule: formatting never changes what a document means.

Prettier moves the HTML block to the margin, out of the list item, and indents its later lines past the box: each pass adds 4 more spaces.

Input:

````markdown
- [ ] a

  <div>x
  y</div>
````

Prettier:

````markdown
- [ ] a

<div>x
    y</div>
````

mdtidy:

````markdown
- [ ] a

  <div>x
  y</div>
````

## An indented line that would open a block keeps its indent

`continuation`. Kind: meaning. Luke's rule: formatting never changes what a document means.

Without the indent, the fence, thematic break, or HTML tag opens a block and ends the paragraph.

Input:

````markdown
text
    ```
````

Prettier:

````markdown
text
```
````

mdtidy:

````markdown
text
    ```
````

## Link targets stay as written where Prettier's form reads differently

`link-target`. Kind: meaning. Luke's rule: formatting never changes what a document means.

Prettier writes the parsed URL. An unbalanced `(` then ends the link, and a backslash, `<`, `>`, or an entity changes the target.

Input:

````markdown
[a](a\(b)

[c](<a<b>)
````

Prettier:

````markdown
[a](a(b)

[c](<a<b>)
````

mdtidy:

````markdown
[a](a\(b)

[c](<a<b>)
````

## An emphasis mark right after `*` is `_`

`emphasis`. Kind: meaning. Luke's rule: formatting never changes what a document means.

Prettier writes `*`, which merges into `***` and nests the other way.

Input:

````markdown
x ***_a_*** y
````

Prettier:

````markdown
x _***a***_ y
````

mdtidy:

````markdown
x _**_a_**_ y
````

## A code span over two lines keeps its second line as written

`code-span`. Kind: meaning. Luke's rule: formatting never changes what a document means.

Prettier writes it from the parsed value, without the container's indent or `>`, so the second line leaves the list item or quote.

Input:

````markdown
- a `x
  y` z
````

Prettier:

````markdown
- a `x
y` z
````

mdtidy:

````markdown
- a `x
  y` z
````

## A blank line before a nested list stays when it is all that keeps the item loose

`nested-blank`. Kind: layout. Not signed off yet: ask Luke.

Prettier drops it and adds one after the item's first line instead. Both read the same; mdtidy keeps the source's choice.

Input:

````markdown
- a
  > q

  - b
````

Prettier:

````markdown
- a

  > q
  - b
````

mdtidy:

````markdown
- a

  > q

  - b
````

## With `wrap: never`, the line after a hard break in a footnote keeps its indent

`footnote-never` (`wrap: never`, width 80). Kind: layout. Not signed off yet: ask Luke.

Prettier drops the indent. It reads the same as a lazy line, but worse.

Input:

````markdown
[^1]: one\
    two
````

Prettier:

````markdown
[^1]: one\
two
````

mdtidy:

````markdown
[^1]: one\
    two
````

## Filling never starts a line with a tag that opens an HTML block

`wrap-html` (`wrap: always`, width 20). Kind: meaning. Luke's rule: formatting never changes what a document means.

Prettier breaks before `<div>`, `<script>`, or `<!--`, which then opens an HTML block. mdtidy moves the word before it down too, as Prettier does for `>` and list markers.

Input:

````markdown
one two three four <div>x</div> five six.
````

Prettier:

````markdown
one two three four
<div>x</div> five
six.
````

mdtidy:

````markdown
one two three
four <div>x</div>
five six.
````

## A paragraph's first line is never a tag alone

`wrap-first-tag` (`wrap: always`, width 20). Kind: meaning. Luke's rule: formatting never changes what a document means.

A lone complete tag on the first line starts an HTML block (CommonMark type 7), so the paragraph turns into raw HTML.

Input:

````markdown
<span title="aaaaaaaa"> <b>x</b> words words
````

Prettier:

````markdown
<span title="aaaaaaaa">
<b>x</b> words words
````

mdtidy:

````markdown
<span title="aaaaaaaa"> <b>x</b>
words words
````

## A line break between Chinese or Japanese and Latin text joins as a space

`wrap-cj-latin` (`wrap: always`, width 20). Kind: meaning. Luke's rule: formatting never changes what a document means.

Prettier joins with nothing when the paragraph mostly has no such spaces, which removes a space that renders.

Input:

````markdown
日本語の文
English words
````

Prettier:

````markdown
日本語の文English
words
````

mdtidy:

````markdown
日本語の文 English
words
````

## A line break between Chinese or Japanese and an emoji joins with nothing

`wrap-cj-emoji` (`wrap: always`, width 20). Kind: meaning. Luke's rule: formatting never changes what a document means.

Both are wide, so CSS renders the break as nothing. Prettier treats the emoji as Latin text and may write a space, which renders.

Input:

````markdown
日本語の文
✅ 完了
````

Prettier:

````markdown
日本語の文 ✅ 完了
````

mdtidy:

````markdown
日本語の文✅ 完了
````

## A line break between wide characters in a link label stays

`wrap-label` (`wrap: always`, width 20). Kind: meaning. Luke's rule: formatting never changes what a document means.

Joining with nothing would change the label so it no longer matches its definition, and Prettier's space renders where the break does not.

Input:

````markdown
[ウィ
キペディア]

[ウィ キペディア]: /w
````

Prettier:

````markdown
[ウィ キペディア]

[ウィ キペディア]:
  /w
````

mdtidy:

````markdown
[ウィ
キペディア]

[ウィ キペディア]:
  /w
````

## After an atom whose last line is past the width, the next word starts a new line

`wrap-atom` (`wrap: always`, width 20). Kind: layout. Not signed off yet: ask Luke.

Prettier measures the atom's first line only and keeps the next word beside it.

Input:

````markdown
a <span
  title="a very long attribute value">b</span> c d
````

Prettier:

````markdown
a <span
  title="a very long attribute value">b</span> c
d
````

mdtidy:

````markdown
a <span
  title="a very long attribute value">b</span>
c d
````
